nodes.summary: A probability measure $\mu$ with $\mu \ll \delta_{x_0}$ equals $\delta_{x_0}$: it gives no mass to $X \setminus \{x_0\}$.
nodes.title: Probability measures dominated by a Dirac mass

For every smooth ($C^\infty$) positive $f$ with $\int f \, d\mu = 1$, writing $\nu = f \mu$, that is $H \le W \sqrt{I}$ for the relative entropy $H = \operatorname{KL}(\nu \,\|\, \mu)$, the Wasserstein distance $W$ and the relative Fisher…
nodes.title: HWI inequality

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or on any finite-dimensional real inner product space). For every smooth ($C^\infty$) positive $f$ with $\int f \, d\gamma = 1$, the left side being the relative entropy $\operatorname{KL}(f\gamma \,\|\, \gamma)$. nodes.title: Gross' logarithmic Sobolev inequality

nodes.summary: For $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ on a metric space, the local Lipschitz constant is the upper limit over $y \ne x$, equal to $0$ at isolated points. For a $C^1$ function on a Riemannian manifold it is the norm of the gradient. It is the notion of gradient in which Gigli and Ledoux state the logarithmic Sobolev inequality on metric measure spaces.
nodes.title: Local Lipschitz constant (slope)

nodes.summary: For every $\alpha$, the Dirac mass $\delta_{x_0}$ satisfies the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant $\alpha$: a density with $\int f \, d\delta_{x_0} = 1$ has $f(x_0) = 1$, so $f \delta_{x_0} = \delta_{x_0}$ and the entropy vanishes. This is a non-vacuity check for the definition.
nodes.title: Dirac masses satisfy the logarithmic Sobolev inequality

nodes.summary: A measure $m$ on a metric space satisfies the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant $\alpha$ if for every nonnegative Lipschitz function $f$ with $\int f \, dm = 1$, where $|\nabla f|$ is the local Lipschitz constant and $\int f \log f \, dm = \operatorname{Ent}_m(f m)$ is the relative entropy of $f m$ with respect to $m$ (Mathlib's Kullback–Leibler divergence, valued in $[0, \infty]$). The right side is the…
nodes.title: Logarithmic Sobolev inequality

nodes.summary: For every $C > 0$, $\delta_{x_0}$ satisfies Talagrand's inequality with constant $C$: $\operatorname{KL}(\mu \,\|\, \delta_{x_0}) = \infty$ unless $\mu = \delta_{x_0}$, and $W_2(\delta_{x_0}, \delta_{x_0}) = 0$. With the log-Sobolev counterpart for Dirac masses this shows that the hypotheses of the Otto–Villani theorem are satisfiable.
nodes.title: Dirac masses satisfy the Talagrand inequality

nodes.title: Otto–Villani theorem

nodes.summary: A probability measure $m$ on a metric space satisfies Talagrand's inequality with constant $C$ if for every probability measure $\mu$, where $W_2$ is the quadratic Wasserstein distance. In Villani's notation $T_2(\lambda)$ is the case $C = 2/\lambda$; the standard Gaussian satisfies it with $C = 2$ (Talagrand's transport inequality for the Gaussian measure).
nodes.title: Talagrand's quadratic transport-cost inequality

nodes.summary: If $m$ satisfies Talagrand's inequality with constant $C$, then for every probability measure $\mu$, because $W_1 \le W_2$. This is the $T_1$ form of the transport inequality, the form that controls integrals of Lipschitz functions.
